COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPSS No. 244 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing
Counsel for the State/respondent nos. 1 to 3.
3. Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for
respondent no. 4.
4. By the instant petition the petitioner is
praying for the following reliefs:
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding/directing
the respondent nos. 3 & 4 to correct the name of
the petitioner as Smt. Savitri Devi in the
pension application form/pension record.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding/directing
the respondents to issue family pension to the
petitioner and further be pleased to direct the
respondents to give the arrears of the pension
along with 18% annual interest till the date of
its realization. "
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that the petitioner's husband, who was serving as
Peon died on 26.04.2024. He submits that in the
service record of the petitioner's husband the
petitioner's name being a nominee and wife of the
deceased employee is correctly shown as Smt.
Savitri Devi; however, subsequently, due to a
clerical mistake of the office concerned in the
documents, which was submitted for grant of
family pension, the name is incorrectly mentioned
as Sumitra Devi.
6. He submits that not only in the service
record of the deceased employee but in other
documents like family register, Aadhar card, Pan
Card the name is shown as Savitri Devi.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent have not
disputed this fact that in the service record and
other documents the name of the petitioner is
shown as Smt. Savitri Devi; however, due to some
inadvertence and clerical mistake the name has

2025:UHC:1415
been shown as Sumitra Devi.
8. Since, this appears to be a clerical mistake
and if it is a clerical mistake it has to be rectified
without any delay.
9. Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for
respondent no. 4, have not disputed this fact that
in the service record of the deceased employee the
petitioner's name has rightly shown as Savitri
Devi as nominee of the deceased.
10. Since, it appears to be a clerical mistake and
it has to be rectified; therefore, the respondent no.
4 is directed to sent the necessary documents and
recommendation for rectification of the name of
the petitioner positively within a week and
thereafter within two weeks the respondent nos. 1
to 3 will rectify it in all the documents including
the pension papers and grant the family pension
without any delay.
11. It is made clear that this entire exercise shall
be completed positively within three weeks.
12. Subject to the direction as made above, the
writ petition is disposed of finally.
